questions.question: What is the routine called that executes when an interrupt fires?
questions.explanation: When an interrupt occurs, the CPU pauses the main program and jumps to the Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) to handle the event.

questions.question: What are the two signal lines used by the I2C protocol?
questions.explanation: I2C uses SDA (Serial Data) for bidirectional data and SCL (Serial Clock) for synchronization between master and slaves.

questions.question: What mechanism lets a microcontroller respond to events immediately instead of continuously polling?
questions.explanation: Interrupts let the hardware signal the CPU when an event occurs, so the processor can react instantly rather than wasting cycles polling.

questions.question: What low-power state do microcontrollers enter to conserve energy when idle?
questions.explanation: Sleep or low-power modes halt the CPU core and shut down unused peripherals, drastically cutting current draw until a wake-up event occurs.

questions.question: What property of an RTOS guarantees responses within bounded, predictable time?
questions.explanation: Determinism means the RTOS guarantees worst-case response times for tasks and interrupts, which is essential for real-time correctness.

questions.question: Which serial protocol offers higher speeds and full-duplex transfer than I2C?
questions.explanation: SPI uses separate MOSI and MISO lines for simultaneous full-duplex transfer and typically runs at much higher clock rates than I2C.

questions.question: What UART parameter, measured in bits per second, must match on both communicating devices?
questions.explanation: Because UART is asynchronous, both ends must be configured to the same baud rate so bits are sampled at the correct times.

questions.question: What technique emulates analog output levels by varying the duty cycle of a digital signal?
questions.explanation: PWM switches a pin between high and low at a fixed frequency; the duty cycle determines the effective average voltage seen by the load.

questions.question: What type of non-volatile memory typically stores firmware on a microcontroller?
questions.explanation: On-chip flash retains the program without power and can be electrically erased and reprogrammed during updates.

questions.question: What technique filters out spurious transitions from a mechanical switch?
questions.explanation: Switch contacts physically bounce for a few milliseconds; debouncing — via RC circuits or software timing — ensures a single clean transition is registered.

questions.question: What term describes embedded software that runs directly on hardware without an operating system?
questions.explanation: Bare-metal firmware runs with no OS layer — the main loop and ISRs interact with hardware registers directly for minimal overhead.

questions.question: Which SPI signal line selects which slave device is being addressed?
questions.explanation: The master asserts a Chip Select (or Slave Select) line for the target slave; SPI has no addressing, so each slave needs its own select line.

questions.question: What is the term for delivering firmware updates to a device wirelessly?
questions.explanation: Over-the-Air (OTA) updates push new firmware to devices over Wi-Fi, cellular, or other wireless links without physical access.

questions.question: What RTOS scheduling approach lets higher-priority tasks interrupt running lower-priority tasks?
questions.explanation: Under preemptive scheduling the kernel immediately switches to the highest-priority ready task, guaranteeing urgent tasks meet their deadlines.

questions.question: What unique identifier allows multiple devices to share a single I2C bus?
questions.explanation: Each I2C device is assigned a unique 7-bit (or 10-bit) address, and the master prefixes every transaction with the target's address.
